name: GHRP-5
lead: GHRP-5 is a synthetic growth hormone-releasing peptide, also referred to in the literature as the Momany peptide.[1] Analytical papers group it with GHRP-1, -2, -4 and -6 as synthetic met-enkephalin analogues with unnatural D-amino acids designed to stimulate growth hormone release.[2]
Published work on GHRP-5 is sparse: anti-doping chemistry, peptide-handling studies, and a laboratory study of its prolactin-releasing activity. No human clinical studies were found.

paras: GHRP-5 is classed as an agonist of the ghrelin/growth hormone secretagogue receptor.[4] An experimental study in Biocell reported prolactin-releasing activity of GHRP-5 on lactotroph cells in vivo and in vitro.[1] A 2026 study in Chirality examined the secondary structure, thermal stability and model-membrane interactions of GHRPs.[5]

Anti-doping laboratories have published urine screening methods covering GHRP-5, and a 2017 paper used GHRP-5 as one of four doping-relevant model peptides in a study of surface adsorption during analysis.[2][3][6] The peptides are described as orally active, and the established growth hormone test does not detect their use.[7]

card.summary: The "Momany peptide": a GH-releasing peptide with lab and anti-doping papers but no human trials.
card.note: Prohibited in competitive sport; no human clinical studies found.

quick.overview:
GHRP-5 is a synthetic peptide in the growth hormone-releasing peptide family, also called the Momany peptide, and is discussed in muscle-building contexts.

The literature is limited to anti-doping chemistry and a few laboratory studies. No human clinical studies were found.
quick.mechanism: It is classed as an agonist of the ghrelin/growth hormone secretagogue receptor, and one laboratory study reported it also releases prolactin.
quick.risks: No human safety data were found. It is on the World Anti-Doping Agency prohibited list and is not an approved medicine.
